en: Dhātukathā 2 Niddesa 2.2.
The Second Method: Exposition of Terms Regarding the Included and the Unincluded.
Those phenomena associated with the eye-base … those phenomena associated with the tangible-object-base … those phenomena associated with the eye-element …

Regarding those phenomena included in the tangible element (*phoṭṭhabbadhātu*) by way of inclusion in the aggregates (*khandha*), but not included by way of inclusion in the bases (*āyatana*) or not included by way of inclusion in the elements (*dhātu*): by how many aggregates, by how many bases, and by how many elements are those phenomena not included?
Those phenomena are not included by four aggregates, two bases, and eight elements.
Regarding those phenomena [included] in the eye-consciousness element (*cakkhuviññāṇadhātu*)...
Those phenomena associated with the ear-consciousness element … those phenomena associated with the nose-consciousness element … those phenomena associated with the tongue-consciousness element …

Those phenomena that are included in the body-consciousness element … those phenomena that are included in the mind-element … those phenomena that are included in the mind-consciousness element by way of inclusion in the aggregates, but are not included in the inclusion of the bases, nor included in the inclusion of the elements … [and so on] …
Those phenomena are not included within the four aggregates, the eleven bases, or the twelve elements.
Those phenomena that [are associated] with the eye faculty … those phenomena that [are associated] with the ear faculty …
Those phenomena [perceived] by the nose-faculty … those phenomena [perceived] by the tongue-faculty … those phenomena [perceived] by the body-faculty …
Those phenomena associated with the female faculty (*itthindriya*) … and those phenomena associated with the male faculty (*purisindriya*),

which are included by the inclusion of aggregates (*khandha-saṅgaha*) but not included by the inclusion of bases (*āyatana-saṅgaha*) nor included by the inclusion of elements (*dhātu-saṅgaha*) … [and so on] … those phenomena are not included by four aggregates, two bases, and eight elements.

Those phenomena that, by way of non-percipient existence (asaññābhava) … or by way of one-aggregate existence (ekavokārabhava), are included under the classification of aggregates (khandha-saṅgaha) but not included under the classification of bases (āyatana-saṅgaha) or the classification of elements (dhātu-saṅgaha) … those phenomena are not included under four aggregates, three bases, and nine elements.
Those phenomena that are associated with lamentation...
those phenomena that are visible and impinging which are included by the inclusion of aggregates, but not included by the inclusion of bases, nor included by the inclusion of elements...
those phenomena are not included by four aggregates, two bases, and eight elements.
Those phenomena which, among the non-demonstrable and resistant phenomena, are included by the inclusion of aggregates but not included by the inclusion of bases or the inclusion of elements—
those phenomena are not included by four aggregates, ten bases, and sixteen elements. Those phenomena which, among the demonstrable phenomena,
are included by the inclusion of aggregates but not included by the inclusion of bases or the inclusion of elements— [and so forth].
Those phenomena are not included within four aggregates, two bases, and eight elements.
Regarding those phenomena which, among the resistant phenomena...

among the derived phenomena, are included by the inclusion of aggregates but are not included by the inclusion of bases and are not included by the inclusion of elements: by how many aggregates, by how many bases, and by how many elements are those phenomena not included?
Those states are not included within four aggregates, eleven bases, and seventeen elements.
Ten bases, seventeen elements,
seven faculties, non-percipient existence, and one-aggregate existence [are not included].
Lamentation is both visible and impinging;
furthermore, it is also invisible and impinging.
This is the second exposition of the included and the un-included.
